content: For residential buildings up to 2 storeys on ordinary soil, minimum foundation depth is typically 1.2 to 1.5 meters below ground level, adjusted for soil bearing capacity and local water table conditions.
Minimum habitable room area is 9.5 sq m with a width not less than 2.4 m. Kitchen minimum area is 5.5 sq m. Bathroom minimum area is 1.8 sq m.
Front setback for residential plots is typically 3m for plots under 200 sq m; side and rear setbacks are commonly 1.5m to 3m depending on building height.

For flat roofs, minimum room height (floor to underside of slab) is 2.75m for pitched roofs on average; minimum clear head room under a beam or eave is 2.4m; air-conditioned rooms require a minimum height of 2.4m to the lowest point of the AC duct or false ceiling.

A habitable room (bedroom/living room) must have a minimum area of 9.5 sq m with minimum width 2.4m if it's the only room. Where there are two rooms, one must be at least 9.5 sq m and the other at least 7.5 sq m, both with minimum width 2.1m.
Kitchen height (floor to underside of slab) must be at least 2.75m, except locally reduced for a floor trap serving the upper floor.

A kitchen with a separate dining area must be at least 5.0 sq m with minimum width 1.8m. If a separate store is provided, kitchen area can reduce to 4.5 sq m. A combined kitchen-cum-dining space must be at least 7.5 sq m with minimum width 2.1m.
Every kitchen must have an impermeable (waterproof) floor, a sink connected via trapped drainage, and a window/ventilator sized per code, plus a flue if needed for exhaust.
Bathroom or water-closet (toilet) height, floor to underside of ceiling, must be at least 2.1m.

A bathroom must be at least 1.8 sq m with minimum width 1.2m. A separate water-closet must be at least 1.1 sq m with minimum width 0.9m. A combined bathroom+WC must be at least 2.8 sq m with minimum width 1.2m.

Every bathroom/WC must have at least one wall open to external air, a water-tight floor with slope toward the drain, impervious wall finish up to at least 1m height, and must not be located directly above/below a kitchen.
A ledge or loft in a habitable room must not cover more than 25 percent of the room's floor area and must not obstruct ventilation. Minimum head-room for a loft is 2.2m; maximum loft height is 1.5m.

Mezzanine floor minimum height is 2.2m. If used as a living space, minimum size is 9.5 sq m, and total mezzanine area in a building cannot exceed one-third of the plinth (ground floor footprint) area. A mezzanine cannot be used as a kitchen or later enclosed into an unventilated room.
A store room must have a minimum height of 2.2m and minimum area of 3 sq m in a residential building.
Garage minimum height is 2.4m. A private garage must be at least 3.0m × 6.0m.
A basement must have minimum 2.4m height (floor to underside of slab/ceiling), adequate ventilation matching the occupancy's byelaw requirements, and cannot be used for residential purposes.
The building line must be set back at least 3m from internal means of access (internal roads) within a layout/plot, subject to further provisions.

source: NBC 2016 Cl.4.3 - Minimum Access Road Width
content: No development on a plot is permitted unless it is accessible by a public street of width not less than 6m. Width of means of access required generally increases with the length of the access road, per Table 1 of the code.

source: NBC 2016 Table 1 - Access Width by Length
content: Minimum width of means of access scales with its length: 6.0m width for up to 75m length, 7.5m for up to 150m, 9.0m for up to 250m, 12.0m for up to 400m, 18.0m for up to 1000m, and 24.0m for over 1000m. If development is only on one side, the prescribed width may be reduced by 1m.

Minimum footpath width is 1.8m generally, 2.5m for commercial/mixed-use areas, 3.5-4.5m for shopping frontages, and up to 4m for high-intensity commercial areas. Footpaths must be level, non-slip, continuous, and include tactile paving and kerb ramps for accessibility.
The building line must be set back at least 3m from internal means of access (internal roads) within a layout/plot.

source: NBC 2016 Cl.8.2.1.1 - Front Open Space by Road Width
content: Minimum front open space depends on the width of the road the plot fronts: 1.5m minimum for roads up to 7.5m wide (buildings up to 7m height only), 3.0m for roads 7.5-18m, 4.5m for roads 18-30m, and 6.0m for roads above 30m wide.

Every residential building must have a rear open space with an average width of at least 3.0m, and never less than 1.8m at any point. For plots with depth under 9m and buildings up to 7m height, rear open space may be reduced to 1.5m. Corner plots under 300 sq m need minimum 2.4m rear open space.

Detached buildings need a minimum 3.0m open space on both sides (reducible to 1.5m for buildings up to 7m height on plots with frontage under 12m). Semi-detached buildings need minimum 3.0m open space on one side (reducible to 1.5m under similar conditions). Row-type (terraced) buildings require no side open space at all.

source: NBC 2016 Table 4 - Side/Rear Open Space by Height
content: For buildings above 10m height, minimum side and rear open space scales with building height: 3m for 10m height, 5m for 15m, 6m for 18m, 7m for 21m, 8m for 24m, 9m for 27m, 10m for 30m, 11m for 35m, 12m for 40m, 13m for 45m, 14m for 50m, 16m for 55m, 17m for 70m, 18m for 120m, and 20m above 120m. Buildings above 24m also require minimum 6m front open space.

source: NBC 2016 Cl.8.2.5 - Interior Courtyard and Ventilation Shaft
content: Where a room's only light/ventilation source is an inner courtyard, minimum courtyard width is 3m. Where a ventilation shaft serves bathrooms/WCs, minimum shaft size scales with building height: 1.2 sq m for buildings up to 10m, 2.8 sq m for 12m, 4.0 sq m for 18m, 5.4 sq m for 24m, 8.0 sq m for 30m, and 9.0 sq m above 30m — with minimum shaft dimension also increasing accordingly.

source: NBC 2016 Table 6 - FAR for Group Housing
content: Floor Area Ratio (FAR) for group housing scales with net residential density: examples include FAR 0.50 at 25 dwelling units/hectare, FAR 1.00 at 100 units/hectare, FAR 2.00 at 200 units/hectare, up to FAR 4.00 at 400 units/hectare — exact ratios vary by local development authority and this table should be cross-checked against local byelaws.

The plinth of a building must not be less than 450mm above surrounding ground level to ensure adequate site drainage. Interior courtyards and covered parking areas must be raised at least 150mm above the determining ground level.

Chimneys must be built at least 0.9m above flat roofs, with the top not below the adjacent parapet wall. For sloping roofs, chimney top must be at least 0.6m above the ridge of the roof it penetrates.
Parapet walls and handrails on roof terraces, balconies, and verandahs must be between 1.0m and 1.2m in height from the finished floor level.

A cabin (small partitioned space within a larger room) must be at least 3.0 sq m with minimum width 1.0m. Clear passage width within divided cabin space must be at least 0.75m, and the farthest point in a cabin must be within 18.5m of an exit.

Maximum boundary/compound wall height is 1.5m above the front street centre line, extendable to 2.4m if the top 0.9m is open-type construction (e.g. railings), subject to Authority approval. Corner plots must restrict wall height to 0.75m for 10m along the front and side near intersections, for visibility/safety.

source: NBC 2016 Cl.12.14 - Well Location and Requirements
content: A well for drinking/domestic water must be located at least 15m from any ash pit, refuse pit, or privy, and at least 18m from any cess pit or soakway/borehole latrine, on ground upslope from such contamination sources. Minimum internal well diameter is 1m.

Note: staircase dimension requirements (tread, riser, width, landing) are governed by NBC 2016 Part 4 'Fire and Life Safety', not Part 3. Common practice for residential staircases: tread depth 250-300mm, riser height 150-190mm, minimum flight width 900mm-1m for private stairs, with a landing required after every 12-15 risers. These figures should be verified against Part 4 directly rather than treated as confirmed NBC citations from this source.

Exit capacity is measured in units of 250mm clear width; clear widths less than 250mm don't count toward exit width at all. This determines how many people a stairway, corridor, or doorway can safely evacuate.

source: NBC 2016 Table 4 (Part 4) - Exit Capacity by Occupancy
content: Width-per-person for means of egress varies by occupancy type: residential/educational/mercantile/industrial need 10mm per person for stairways and 6.5mm for level components (corridors/ramps); institutional and business occupancies need 15mm for stairways and 13mm for level components; hazardous occupancies need 18mm for stairways and 10mm for level components.

A dead-end corridor (one with only one exit direction) creates evacuation risk. Buildings should be planned so occupants have at least two direction choices to reach an exit wherever practical, per the code's exit access planning principles.

For buildings 15-30m tall, internal staircases without external walls generally require pressurization for smoke control; buildings over 30m need pressurized or cross-ventilated staircases. Naturally ventilated staircases need at least 0.5 sq m opening at each landing in an external wall.

source: NBC 2016 Table 7 - Fire Equipment by Building Type
content: Required firefighting equipment (extinguishers, hose reels, wet risers, sprinklers, fire alarms) scales with building height and occupancy type — e.g. buildings 15-30m need fire extinguishers, hose reels, wet risers, and automatic detection/alarm systems as standard; requirements increase further above 30m. Exact equipment lists should be checked against the full table for the specific occupancy class.
